project.name: FreeType 2
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected here is the checkout under `gt_results/arvo_42539076/_work/src/freetype2` at `27fee7f8c6ae75e066b5a23472b33925c6e8b1e0`; its `src/truetype/ttgxvar.c:2144` line map matches both the saved default crash trace and Stage 01's rebuilt ASan reproduction. ARVO metadata separately reports `7d7aae1de3e2aea5bad2e92b0f9d074bd5130ecd` / `7bbb91fbf47fc0775cc9705673caf0c47a81f94b`, and the packaged `patch.diff` is that later metadata-branch fix. This staged checkout is a different pre-fix branch whose `sfnt_init_face()` still zeroes `num_instances` for any CFF face before the default-instance synthesis block, but it reaches the same `TT_Get_MM_Var` named-instance write sink.
project.fixed_commit_note: The packaged `patch.diff` does not apply line-for-line to the staged checkout because it was taken from the later metadata branch, where the same `num_instances = 0` decision had already been narrowed once. It is still source-relevant supporting evidence: it tightens the same CFF-gating obligation by preserving named instances when `glyf` or `CFF2` has precedence.

staged_source_snapshot.description: All source locations below are anchored to this exact staged vulnerable checkout.

classification.classification_note: The public issue text labels this sample a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 4. The preserved Stage 01 symptom is `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / `wild-addr-write` at `TT_Get_MM_Var`, but the source-level defect is the same out-of-bounds named-instance write: the staged `sfnt_init_face()` stores only one synthesized named instance while `TT_Get_MM_Var()` later writes coordinates for more real `fvar` instances than that allocation accounts for.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42539076 (freetype2): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 4 found by fuzz target ftfuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42539076
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` caused by a WRITE at `src/truetype/ttgxvar.c:2144` in the staged FreeType checkout `27fee7f8c6ae75e066b5a23472b33925c6e8b1e0`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `7d7aae1de3e2aea5bad2e92b0f9d074bd5130ecd`. The exact raw `poc` is passed straight to `FT_New_Memory_Face`, where `sfnt_init_face()` reads a valid `fvar` header and marks the face as variation-capable. In this staged branch, `sfnt_init_face()` then zeroes the parsed named-instance count as soon as a `CFF` table is present; the later default-instance synthesis can recover only a single stored instance, so `face->root.style_flags >> 16` becomes 1 even though `TT_Get_MM_Var()` later reparses more than one real named instance from the same `fvar` table. `setIntermediateAxis()` still reaches `FT_Get_MM_Var()`, and that function allocates and initializes storage for only one `FT_Var_Named_Style` before looping over the real `fvar_head.instanceCount`. On a later loop iteration `ns` has advanced past `namedstyle[0]`, `ns->coords` is read from out-of-bounds pseudo-`FT_Var_Named_Style` bytes, and `*c = FT_GET_LONG()` writes a 32-bit coordinate through the resulting invalid pointer. The packaged `patch.diff` is the later metadata-branch tightening of the same `num_instances = 0` decision with `glyf`/`CFF2` precedence; Stage 01 did not preserve a fixed-build rerun, so that patch is supporting source evidence rather than dynamic remediation proof.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled variation header. This block materializes the font's `fvar` instance metadata, including the named-instance count that later disagrees with the single synthesized count stored in `style_flags`.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is passed as one raw in-memory file because `src/tools/ftfuzzer/ftfuzzer.cc:203-204` falls back to `files.emplace_back( data, data + size )` when the input is not recognized as an uncompressed tar archive. `sfnt_init_face()` then reads the `fvar` header fields directly from those attacker-controlled bytes.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. On a post-`namedstyle[0]` iteration, `c` is an invalid `FT_Fixed*` loaded from out-of-bounds pseudo-`FT_Var_Named_Style` storage, and this statement writes the next 32-bit named-instance coordinate through it.
sink.note: Both the saved default trace and Stage 01's rebuilt run report `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / WRITE at this exact line with stack `TT_Get_MM_Var -> setIntermediateAxis -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the exact staged vulnerable source, the CFF gate clears the parsed named-instance count before later code stores it in the face object, even though later variation handling can still reach `TT_Get_MM_Var()` on the same font.
root_cause.note: Because this staged branch performs the CFF check before default-instance synthesis, later code can recover only a single synthetic instance rather than the real `fvar` count. The packaged metadata-branch `patch.diff` tightens this same zeroing decision by adding `glyf`/`CFF2` precedence checks.

tainted_value_origin.description: This commits the vulnerability-relevant stored instance count into the face object. After steps 3-4, `face->root.style_flags >> 16` is 1 even though `TT_Get_MM_Var()` later reparses more than one real named instance from the same font.

parser_admitted.description: The `fvar` header passes the staged structural checks, so the face is marked as carrying variation data and later MM-specific paths remain reachable.

evidence_limitations: The exact staged vulnerable source is checkout `27fee7f8c6ae75e066b5a23472b33925c6e8b1e0`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit` `7d7aae1de3e2aea5bad2e92b0f9d074bd5130ecd`. The trace is grounded in the staged checkout because its line map matches the saved ASan crash.

The packaged `patch.diff` is source-relevant but belongs to a later metadata branch. Stage 01 did not preserve a fixed-build rerun, so `patch_resolves` below remains `false` even though the patch supports the missing CFF/CFF2 precedence obligation.

The saved artifacts prove that `setIntermediateAxis()` reached `FT_Get_MM_Var()`, but with `runtime_disambiguation` disabled they do not distinguish which internal face-flag branch originally set `FT_FACE_FLAG_MULTIPLE_MASTERS` before that call. That ambiguity is not needed to close the write-side chain.

if ( face->goto_table( face, TTAG_fvar, stream, &fvar_len ) ||
     fvar_len < 20                                          ||

fine_trace.note: Source. `sfnt_init_face()` reads the attacker-controlled `fvar` header and materializes the font's named-instance metadata, including the instance count that later disagrees with the single synthesized count stored in `style_flags`.

fine_trace.code:
if ( version != 0x00010000UL                    ||
     axis_size != 20                            ||
     num_axes == 0                              ||
     num_axes > 0x3FFE                          ||
     !( instance_size == 4 + 4 * num_axes ||
        instance_size == 6 + 4 * num_axes )     ||
     num_instances > 0x7EFF                     ||
     offset + axis_size * num_axes + instance_size * num_instances > fvar_len )
  num_instances = 0;
else
  face->variation_support |= TT_FACE_FLAG_VAR_FVAR;
fine_trace.note: The staged structural checks accept the parsed `fvar` header, so the face is marked as carrying variation data instead of being rejected as a malformed non-MM font.

depends_on.via: version, offset, num_axes, axis_size, num_instances, instance_size

fine_trace.note: Root cause. The exact staged vulnerable branch clears the parsed named-instance count as soon as a `CFF` table is present. This happens before the later default-instance synthesis block, so the real `fvar` count is lost here.

Because step 3 forced `num_instances = 0`, the scan over existing named instances executes zero iterations and the `if ( i == num_instances )` test immediately synthesizes exactly one default instance. The stored count is therefore repaired only from 0 to 1, not back to the real `fvar` named-instance count.
The face object now carries a stored named-instance count of 1 in `style_flags`, and later code reuses exactly this stale count to size the `FT_MM_Var` allocation.

Reachability gate. The saved crash stack shows `TT_Get_MM_Var` was called from `setIntermediateAxis`, so this `FT_HAS_MULTIPLE_MASTERS` guard did not return early and the MM API consumed the face carrying step 5's stored count.

Inside `TT_Get_MM_Var()`, FreeType reparses the same attacker-controlled `fvar` header into local `fvar_head`. The real `fvar_head.instanceCount` read here is the loop bound for the later named-instance copy.

fine_trace.code:
num_instances = face->root.style_flags >> 16;

face->blend->mmvar_len =
  sizeof ( FT_MM_Var ) +
  fvar_head.axisCount * sizeof ( FT_Var_Axis ) +
  num_instances * sizeof ( FT_Var_Named_Style ) +
  num_instances * fvar_head.axisCount * sizeof ( FT_Fixed ) +
  5 * fvar_head.axisCount;
fine_trace.note: `TT_Get_MM_Var()` trusts step 5's stored count, so `num_instances` becomes 1 and the packed `FT_MM_Var` allocation reserves space for only one `FT_Var_Named_Style` plus one coordinate array, even though step 7 may have read more real named instances from the font.
Because step 8 set `num_instances = 1`, this loop initializes only `mmvar->namedstyle[0].coords`. No later `FT_Var_Named_Style` entry receives a valid `coords` pointer.

The copy loop still uses step 7's real `fvar_head.instanceCount`, not step 8's stored `num_instances`. Since only `namedstyle[0].coords` was initialized in step 9 and the crash still occurs in this loop, the witness's real `fvar_head.instanceCount` must exceed 1, so some post-first iteration runs with `ns` already beyond the single allocated entry.

On one of the post-first iterations from step 10, `ns` no longer points to a real `FT_Var_Named_Style`. Reading `ns->coords` therefore fetches an invalid destination pointer from out-of-bounds pseudo-structure bytes.

Sink. `FT_GET_LONG()` supplies the next 32-bit named-instance design coordinate and stores it through the invalid pointer from step 11. This matches the saved AddressSanitizer `SEGV` / write at `ttgxvar.c:2144`.

poc.trigger: Running the exact staged raw `poc` through `ftfuzzer` reproduces `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / `wild-addr-write` in `TT_Get_MM_Var` at `src/truetype/ttgxvar.c:2144` while `setIntermediateAxis()` calls `FT_Get_MM_Var()` on the current face.

format.name: raw FreeType font input
format.contract: The exact raw font bytes passed to `FT_New_Memory_Face` must yield a valid `fvar` header, a present `CFF` table, and more than one real named instance, while the staged `sfnt_init_face()` path stores only one synthesized instance in `style_flags`; `setIntermediateAxis()` then reaches `TT_Get_MM_Var()`, whose named-instance loop advances past `namedstyle[0]` and writes through invalid `ns->coords`.
